anomalies.observed: Q1 (AO3401A P-MOSFET, the LTC4412 ideal-diode pass device) has its source (pin 2) on +5V and its drain (pin 3) on USBC_VBUS_IN. The LTC4412 VIN (U6.1) is on USBC_VBUS_IN and its SENSE (U6.6) is on +5V. The FET is therefore oriented with the output side on the source and the input side on the drain, which is the reverse of the standard ideal-diode arrangement.
anomalies.expected: For an LTC4412 ideal-diode OR with a P-channel MOSFET, the source should be on the VIN (USB input) side and the drain on the load side (+5V), with SENSE on the load. The other load switches on this board (Q6 and Q9) follow this source-on-supply orientation: Q6.2 (S) on +5V and Q9.2 (S) on +5V.

evidence.quote: USBC_VBUS_IN [High Power] : J3.A4(VBUS,passive) ... Q1.3(D,passive) R11.1(passive) R64.2(2,passive) U25.5(VBUS,passive) U6.1(VIN,power_in)

anomalies.impact: The power-path FET is mis-oriented relative to the controller. Reverse-current protection and the intended forward path through the PMOS can behave differently from the design intent, which could affect USB power delivery and back-feed protection.

anomalies.observed: Both ISO1050 isolated CAN transceivers have their GND2 pins (pin 5) tied to the main GND net, together with GND1 (pin 4). The isolated-side ground is therefore not separated from the logic ground, and the transceiver provides no galvanic isolation.
anomalies.expected: An isolated CAN transceiver requires a separate isolated ground (GND2) for the bus side, decoupled from the logic ground. The spec describes these as "isolated CAN transceivers" on "two isolated CAN buses".

evidence.quote: GND [High Power] : ... U10.4(GND1,power_in) U10.5(GND2,power_in) U11.4(GND1,power_in) U11.5(GND2,power_in)
two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (`U8`, `U9`) through an isolated CAN transceiver (`U11`/companion)

anomalies.impact: Isolation between the CAN bus and the logic ground is defeated, so ground loops and fault paths from the motor-controller bus can reach the main board and the CM4, which removes the protection the isolated transceiver was meant to provide.

anomalies.observed: The dual LED D30 has its second anode (A2, pin 4) directly on ESTOP_OUT, and its second cathode (K2, pin 2) goes through R60 back to ESTOP_OUT. The LED is therefore connected across a single net and cannot be forward-biased. The library's pin mapping (K1/K2 on pins 1/2, A1/A2 on pins 3/4) also conflicts with the part description, which says cathodes are on pins 1 and 3.
anomalies.expected: Each LED of the dual part should have its anode and cathode on different nets, with the series resistor between the driven node and the cathode. The pin assignment should match the actual LED part.

evidence.quote: D30 | LED_Dual_KKAA | ... | Dual LED, cathodes on pins 1 and 3

anomalies.impact: The E-stop status LED associated with ESTOP_OUT cannot light, and its series resistor R60 loads ESTOP_OUT with no useful function. This would be a user-visible indication failure rather than a safety-loop failure.
